title: The p(doom) database
description: Public, self-stated estimates of the probability that advanced AI causes human extinction or a comparable catastrophe. One row per statement, each with a source. Maintained at pdoomcoin.lol; contributions via GitHub.

entries.name: Roman Yampolskiy
entries.role: AI safety researcher, University of Louisville

entries.name: Louis Berman
entries.role: Former tech CTO; AI x-risk activist
entries.scope: p(doom), as asked on Doom Debates
entries.quote: I'm saying basically it is P(100). Roman Yampolskiy is off by a rounding error.
entries.note: Also: "P(doom) in less than five years, I think is easily P(50)." Concedes ~2% non-doom under pressure.

entries.name: Michael Ellsberg
entries.scope: everyone dies, conditional on a robust ASI being built
entries.horizon: within one to two years of ASI
entries.quote: And so I would say conditional on ASI, my P(Doom) is 99%. I don't know how fast it would happen, one year, two years, maybe immediately.
entries.note: Conditional on ASI arising.

entries.name: Nate Soares
entries.scope: humanity's extinction if current trends continue
entries.quote: at least 95%
entries.note: Originally in The Times (UK), quoted via TASS; conditional on no change of course. Told The Atlantic >50% within his lifetime.

entries.name: Jeremy Gillen
entries.scope: AI doom, conditional on rushing into superintelligence
entries.quote: I don't know, like pretty high. Probably higher than 90%, probably lower than 99%, in that kind of region. This is also conditioning on rushing forward into superintelligence.
entries.note: Says he hasn't put much thought into the number.

entries.name: Connor Leahy
entries.quote: you could be at 99% probability of doom, but have like five or 10% error bars. — Yes, that's kind of my thinking.
entries.note: Host's framing, which he affirmed; "not as pessimistic as Eliezer but pretty close."

entries.name: Steven Byrnes
entries.scope: p(doom), as asked on Doom Debates
entries.quote: I don't know, 90% or something, but I kind of pulled that number out of my ass, so take it for whatever it's worth.
entries.note: Explicitly a rough guess; expects the danger from a future brain-like AGI paradigm, not LLMs.

entries.name: Max Tegmark
entries.role: MIT physicist; president, Future of Life Institute
entries.scope: loss of human control over superintelligence, if no regulation
entries.quote: When I said P(doom) of over 90%, that was if we do no regulation. I am actually quite optimistic because I don't think China will allow a race to superintelligence
entries.note: Conditional on no tough regulation; derived from his MIT paper on scalable oversight failing 92% of the time in the most optimistic scenario.

entries.name: David Duvenaud
entries.role: Professor, University of Toronto; former Anthropic researcher
entries.scope: p(doom), as asked on Doom Debates
entries.quote: So I'd say something around 85%.
entries.note: Clip replayed in the State of the Show episode; originally from his own Doom Debates episode.

entries.name: Dan Hendrycks
entries.quote: As it happens, my p(doom) > 80%, but it has been lower in the past. Two years ago it was ~20%.
entries.note: Says it was ~20% two years earlier.

entries.name: Aella
entries.scope: p(doom), as asked on Doom Debates
entries.quote: Liron: That's why you're saying 75% P(Doom). Aella: Yeah. It's a lot higher than I would like it to be.
entries.note: Figure stated by the host and confirmed by her on air.

entries.name: Zvi Mowshowitz
entries.role: Writer, Don't Worry About the Vase
entries.quote: Nathan: last time we spoke, I believe your p(doom) was 70%. Has it ticked down at all? Zvi: More higher than down from previous assessment, but not enough to move to 0.8, certainly.
entries.note: Up from his 60% of 2023.

entries.name: John Sherman
entries.quote: John starts out at 75%, unrelated to their numbers.
entries.note: From the show's own episode description; transcript not read.

entries.name: Daniel Kokotajlo
entries.quote: I think AI doom is 70% likely and I think people who think it is less than, say, 20% are being very unreasonable
entries.note: Most of his remaining hope is humans coordinating not to build dangerous AI.

entries.name: Justin Helps
entries.quote: If you're talking P(Doom) for all time, I guess I put 70% at 2100 is the number I put in the video. So it's pretty high in the long run, but it's a lot lower in the short run.
entries.note: Much lower short-run figure; episode notes cite 5% by 2040.

entries.name: Marcus Williams
entries.scope: human extinction, if no regulation or slowdown
entries.quote: 70% in the next 3 years if there isn't regulation/slowdown although i think regulation/slowdown is very possible
entries.note: Conditional on no regulation or coordinated slowdown.

entries.name: Zvi Mowshowitz
entries.role: AI writer, Don't Worry About the Vase
entries.quote: So if I have to tell people a number, I am saying 0.6, 60%.
entries.note: Prefers Leike's 10–90% framing. Later reported higher on Doom Debates.

entries.name: Richard Ren
entries.scope: losing ~99.9% of humanity's potential value (extinction or permanent disempowerment)
entries.quote: Probably around 50 to 65%.
entries.note: Re-confirmed later in the episode after the host misremembered it as 40%.

entries.name: Liv Boeree
entries.scope: p(doom), as asked on Doom Debates
entries.quote: Um, I mean, it's somewhere between five and 99%.
entries.note: Calls it "a hot mess of a probability distribution"; even 5% is unacceptable to her.

entries.name: David Krueger
entries.quote: I think that's more likely than not.

entries.name: Liron Shapira
entries.quote: my P(doom) of 50%

entries.name: Emad Mostaque
entries.scope: existential outcome; AI eliminating humanity to preempt rival AI
entries.quote: My P(Doom) is fifty percent.
entries.note: Elsewhere attaches 10–20 year timelines. Earlier stated the same on X, Dec 2024.

entries.name: Holden Karnofsky
entries.horizon: nearcast: transformative AI developed very soon
entries.quote: I don't currently have much sympathy for someone who's highly confident that AI takeover would or would not happen (that is, for anyone who thinks the odds of AI takeover in this nearcast are under 10% or over 90%).
entries.note: A stated plausible band for a hypothetical scenario, not a point estimate.

entries.name: Jan Leike
entries.scope: a very bad outcome from AI
entries.quote: Rob Wiblin: My guess is that it's more than 10% and less than 90%. Jan Leike: Yeah. That's probably the range I would give too.
entries.note: Range proposed by the host; Leike endorsed it, after saying p(doom) depends on his mood and isn't a useful question.

entries.name: Rob Miles
entries.scope: p(doom), as asked on Doom Debates
entries.quote: I think anyone whose number is below 10% or above 90% is overconfident. I have a ton of model uncertainty here. I think that sort of any number in the 10 to 90% range is plausibly defensible.
entries.note: Agrees when the host places him "in the 50 plus zone", then qualifies that it depends on how humanity responds.

entries.name: Geoffrey Miller
entries.role: Evolutionary psychologist, University of New Mexico
entries.scope: p(doom), as asked on Doom Debates
entries.quote: 50%. But also with broad uncertainty and margins of error. We could push the P(Doom) as low as 5% in this century, and if we were really stupid, we could push it as high as 80%.
entries.note: Contingent on human behavior: 5% to 80% depending on societal response.

entries.name: Tristan Harris
entries.scope: AI kills everybody or destroys >99% of potential value
entries.quote: Liron: So we're talking 50% plus? Tristan: More than 50%.
entries.note: Conditional: "if we don't change course."

entries.name: Geoffrey Irving
entries.role: Former Chief Scientist, UK AI Security Institute
entries.horizon: driven by actions in the next few to 10 years
entries.quote: I think we have a ~50% chance of all dying as a result of superintelligence, mostly due to actions in the next few to 10 years.
entries.note: Explained as the mean of a long-held 10–90% range.

entries.name: Nathan Labenz
entries.quote: I usually answer when people ask this in general is 10 to 90%. And what I mean by that is basically, like, I really have no idea.
entries.note: Puts most weight on the lower end.

entries.name: Paul Christiano
entries.role: Former head of safety, US CAISI; founded ARC
entries.horizon: within 10 years of building powerful AI
entries.quote: Probability that humanity has somehow irreversibly messed up our future within 10 years of building powerful AI: 46%
entries.note: Same post: AI takeover 22%; most humans die within 10 years of powerful AI 20%.

entries.name: Carl Feynman
entries.quote: 43%. 43% P(Doom) means I have... What is that? 57%.
entries.note: Says it was a little higher previously; things improved as more people noticed the problem.

entries.name: Joep Meindertsma
entries.quote: Die mogelijkheid schat hij op 40 procent. „Ik twijfel continu, maar de kans dat het fout gaat is groot”
entries.note: Journalist's paraphrase of his estimate in a profile he reviewed; adds "I doubt constantly, but the chance it goes wrong is large."

entries.name: Eli Lifland
entries.quote: something like 35 to 40% for any AI-mediated existential catastrophe
entries.note: Says he doesn't think much about exact numbers.

entries.name: Scott Alexander
entries.scope: human extinction from unaligned superintelligent AI
entries.quote: if you force me to give an estimate it's probably around 33%; I think it's very plausible that we die, but more likely that we survive (at least for a little while)
entries.note: Given only "if forced"; explicitly not a precise prediction.

entries.name: Avalon Warren
entries.scope: p(doom), as asked on Doom Debates
entries.quote: My P(Doom)'s somewhere between... I think I would wanna go 33.

entries.name: AI safety researchers (survey, n=44)
entries.label: 30% (mean)
entries.scope: existential catastrophe: future value drastically reduced for lack of AI safety research
entries.quote: How likely do you think it is that the overall value of the future will be drastically less than it could have been, as a result of humanity not doing enough technical AI safety research?
entries.note: n=44 of ~117 invited. Mean ~30%, median 20%. Alignment researchers, not general AI researchers.

entries.name: Holly Elmore
entries.scope: 20% extinction; up to 40% worst civilizational tragedies
entries.quote: My pat answer is that it's like 20 to 40% on the worst - the variation is like 20% extinction and then to like 40%, the worst civilizational tragedies, but not everyone dies.
entries.note: For "everyone dies by 2050": closer to 20. Says the number varies day to day.

entries.name: Lumpenspace
entries.quote: If you mean no biological humans exist in the universe, that might be close to 30 maybe.
entries.note: ~0% if doom means nothing of value exists; ~30% only for the no-biological-humans definition.

entries.name: Emmett Shear
entries.role: Co-founder, Twitch; former interim CEO, OpenAI
entries.note: HuffPost paraphrase of a Logan Bartlett Show clip Shear reposted himself, June 2023. No verbatim transcript read.

entries.name: Alex Turner
entries.role: AI safety researcher, formerly Google DeepMind
entries.scope: AI kills at least a billion people
entries.quote: So I operationalize P(Doom) as probability that AI kills at least a billion people by 2050. I put that at, I don't know, 25, 30%.
entries.note: About 10 points technical misalignment, the rest misuse.

entries.name: Shane Legg
entries.role: Co-founder and Chief AGI Scientist, Google DeepMind
entries.scope: human extinction within a year of human-level AI
entries.horizon: within a year of human-level AI
entries.quote: Maybe 5%, maybe 50%. I don't think anybody has a good estimate of this.
entries.note: Written Q&A before DeepMind was founded; no known updated number.

entries.name: Rohin Shah
entries.scope: things going badly due to misalignment
entries.quote: Positions like more than 1% and less than 50% all feel pretty justifiable to me.
entries.note: Refuses a point estimate: "these numbers feel particularly made up."

entries.name: Dario Amodei
entries.quote: There's a 25% chance that things go really, really badly … 75% chance that things go really, really well.
entries.note: Axios AI+ DC Summit. Top of his earlier 10–25% range.

entries.name: Samotsvety forecasters (n=11)
entries.label: 25% (aggregate)
entries.quote: Aggregate 25% probability of misaligned AI takeover by 2100, barring pre-APS-AI catastrophe (individual range 3%–91.5%).
entries.note: Geometric mean of odds after trimming extremes; individual range 3–91.5%.

entries.name: AI safety leaders (CEA Summit on Existential Security 2026, n=59)
entries.role: Centre for Effective Altruism attendee survey
entries.label: 25% (median)
entries.scope: human extinction or permanent disempowerment, all causes
entries.quote: Median 25% (mean 34%) probability of human extinction or permanent human disempowerment before 2100.
entries.note: Range 5–95%; 15% answered 70% or higher.

entries.name: Carl Shulman
entries.role: Independent researcher; advisor to Open Philanthropy
entries.quote: At this point depending on the day I might say one in four or one in five.
entries.note: Would have said ~10% in the 2000s, before deep learning.

entries.name: Yoshua Bengio
entries.quote: I got around, like, 20 per cent probability that it turns out catastrophic.
entries.note: Derived from ~50% chance of human-level AI within a decade and >50% it's turned against humanity at scale.

entries.name: Elon Musk
entries.quote: only a 20% chance of annihilation

entries.name: Dwarkesh Patel
entries.quote: mine literally is a number I kind of pulled out of my ass. I don't know, like 20% or something. And just because that's Carl Shulman's
entries.note: Says the number is borrowed from Carl Shulman.

entries.name: Dario Amodei
entries.quote: a 25% chance that things go really, really badly
entries.note: Clarified on Hard Fork, Feb 2025: "10 to 25% referred to the chance of civilization getting substantially derailed, which is not the same as an AI killing everyone."

entries.name: Liam Robins
entries.quote: My inside-view P(doom) is now 42.22%. With a 60% linear weight on superforecasters, that brings my all-things-considered P(doom) to 17.42%.
entries.note: Up from 3.38% in June 2025.

entries.name: Lina Khan
entries.scope: AI-caused existential catastrophe, as asked by the Hard Fork hosts
entries.quote: no, no, more like 15%
entries.note: Said on NYT Hard Fork after calling herself an optimist. Quote via transcription; audio not checked directly.

entries.name: Neel Nanda
entries.quote: I'm happy to put at least a 1% chance of AI causing human extinction (my fair value is probably 10-20%, with high uncertainty).
entries.note: Written before joining DeepMind; has since said he deliberately doesn't publicize a p(doom).

entries.name: Manifold traders (AI wipes out humanity before 2100, n=816)
entries.label: 13.6% (market)
entries.quote: Market probability 13.6% on 'Will AI wipe out humanity before the year 2100'.
entries.note: Live on the pdoomcoin.lol board. Play-money; YES can never pay out.

entries.name: Vitalik Buterin
entries.quote: About 12% right now.
entries.note: Was 15–16% at the start of 2025 and ~10% earlier. Extinction by 2050 specifically: at least 9%.

entries.name: Evan Hubinger
entries.quote: I personally think it is >10% within the next decade
entries.note: Adds that risk from current models is low.

entries.name: Vitalik Buterin
entries.quote: AI risk 1: existential risk. My p(doom) is around 0.1. You don't have to buy this story, but IMO it's worth worrying about.
entries.note: Stated as 0.1, i.e. 10%, in the thread for his techno-optimism essay.

entries.name: David Sirota
entries.role: Screenwriter, Don't Look Up; journalist, The Lever
entries.scope: p(doom), as asked on Doom Debates
entries.quote: My P(Doom) is way higher than 10%.
entries.note: No upper bound given.

entries.name: Geoffrey Hinton
entries.quote: A 10% chance seems not an unreasonable estimate to me. But nobody really knows how to give a sensible estimate.
entries.note: BBC Newsnight, endorsing Hubinger's framing; said it would be "very foolish to say 1%."

entries.name: Toby Ord
entries.role: Philosopher, Oxford; author of The Precipice
entries.quote: 1 in 10
entries.note: From The Precipice; in 2024 said the estimates are rounded to the nearest factor of 10 and none have moved far.

entries.name: Joe Carlsmith
entries.scope: existential catastrophe from misaligned power-seeking AI
entries.quote: since making this report public in April 2021, my estimate here has gone up, and is now at >10%.
entries.note: Original April 2021 estimate was ~5%.

entries.name: Rohin Shah
entries.scope: AI causes human extinction by adversarially optimizing against humans
entries.quote: an unusually large (90%) chance that AI systems will be safe without additional intervention.
entries.note: Said not to take it too seriously; "might have said 80%, or 95%."

entries.name: Mikita Balesni
entries.quote: i am at OpenAI and i think AI is >10% likely to kill all humans.

entries.name: Victoria Krakovna
entries.quote: I think there is a >10% chance of advanced AI causing human extinction in the next decade

entries.name: Dima Krasheninnikov
entries.quote: believe there's plausibly a ≥10% chance that a future out-of-control AI kills everyone
entries.note: Hedged with "plausibly."

entries.name: Lex Fridman
entries.scope: AGI/ASI destroys all of human civilization
entries.quote: the probability that AGI and then ASI might destroy all of human civilization. I would say my p(doom) is about 10%.
entries.note: Stated while asking Sundar Pichai, who declined to give a number.

entries.name: Dwarkesh Patel
entries.quote: Ten percent or something like that.
entries.note: Lower than his ~20% of Dec 2023.

entries.name: Paul Christiano
entries.scope: catastrophic and irreversible loss of control
entries.quote: If I had to quantify my uncertainty I would estimate an all-things-considered risk of 4% over the next year and 15% over the next three years
entries.note: Personal statement on joining the OpenAI board.

entries.name: Machine learning researchers (survey, n≈2,778)
entries.label: 5–10% (median)
entries.scope: human extinction or similarly permanent and severe disempowerment
entries.quote: The median prediction for extremely bad outcomes, such as human extinction, was 5% (mean 9%)
entries.note: Medians 5–10% and means 9–19% across four question wordings, N up to 2,704. Survey Oct 2023.

entries.name: Nate Silver
entries.quote: My estimate of p(doom) would be considered high by normal person standards but is well in line with the expert consensus, which puts the chances at 5 to 10 percent.
entries.note: Given indirectly: "in line with" the 5–10% consensus rather than a figure of his own.

entries.name: Stephen Casper
entries.role: AI safety researcher, MIT; UK AISI
entries.scope: p(doom), as asked on Doom Debates
entries.quote: I think my P(Doom) lies somewhere between 5% and 10%

entries.name: Katja Grace
entries.quote: My probability on, 'AI destroys the world', is probably something like 7%.
entries.note: Product of written-down component probabilities.

entries.name: Buck Shlegeris
entries.scope: catastrophic misalignment risk after control measures
entries.quote: It would be pretty surprising to me to get under 5%. And suppose we're above 5%: what are we going to do, not deploy the AIs?
entries.note: A lower bound, not a point estimate.

entries.name: Benjamin Mann
entries.quote: somewhere between 0 and 10%
entries.note: Lenny's Podcast; taken from episode summaries, full transcript paywalled.

entries.name: Casey Newton
entries.quote: Tech reporter Casey Newton has a p(doom) score of 5%
entries.note: Reported by Fast Company; not his own words in a transcript.

entries.name: AI researchers (AI Impacts 2022, n=738)
entries.label: 5% (median)
entries.scope: extremely bad long-run outcome of high-level machine intelligence
entries.quote: The median respondent gave a 5% probability that the long-run impact of HLMI on humanity would be 'extremely bad (e.g. human extinction)'.
entries.note: 738 of 4,271 NeurIPS/ICML authors. Mean ~14%. The control-failure variant had a median of 10%.

entries.name: AI researchers (AI Impacts 2016, n=352)
entries.role: Grace et al., When Will AI Exceed Human Performance?
entries.label: 5% (median)
entries.scope: extremely bad long-run outcome of HLMI
entries.quote: the probability was 10% for a bad outcome and 5% for an outcome described as 'Extremely Bad (e.g., human extinction).'
entries.note: Fielded 2016; 352 of 1,634 NIPS/ICML 2015 authors.

entries.name: Manifold traders (AI wipes out humanity before 2030, n=1,117)
entries.label: 5% (market)
entries.quote: Market probability 5% on 'Will AI wipe out humanity before the year 2030?'
entries.note: Play-money; YES can never pay out, so read as a poll biased toward NO.

entries.name: Destiny (Steven Bonnell)
entries.quote: You know what? I'll up it to five percent
entries.note: Closing estimate on the same episode, up from <1%.

entries.name: Kevin Roose
entries.role: Tech columnist, The New York Times; co-host, Hard Fork
entries.scope: AI turns on us and does catastrophic harm
entries.quote: one in twenty chance that AI turns on us and does catastrophic harm
entries.note: Reported secondhand; NYT transcript not read, may be a paraphrase.

entries.name: Robert Wright
entries.scope: no modern humans living decent lives at all
entries.quote: Mm, I don't know, 4 or 5%, which is high for something like that, right?
entries.note: For a broader 'suffering' dystopia within 100 years: "I wish I could say less than 50%, but I'm not sure I can."

entries.name: Quintin Pope
entries.scope: p(doom), as asked on Doom Debates
entries.quote: Well, my P(Doom) is 4%, so yes, both of those things need to be imagined.
entries.note: Debate recorded in 2023 on Twitter Spaces; published on Doom Debates in 2026.

entries.name: Liam Robins
entries.role: Math student, George Washington University; AI policy writer
entries.scope: p(doom), as asked on Doom Debates
entries.quote: My P(doom) is 3.38%. Here's Why.
entries.note: Title of his own post. The host reports he updated toward 8% mid-debate in part 2.

entries.name: Ben Goertzel
entries.label: π%
entries.scope: p(doom), as asked on Doom Debates
entries.quote: I don't think that's a very useful question because we don't have any rational way to estimate that. So if I have to pick a number, I'll come up with π percent.
entries.note: Half-joking; says the question isn't useful. Adds that doom without AGI (nukes, bio, nanotech) is higher than LeCun's figure.

entries.name: Gary Marcus
entries.scope: humans literally go extinct at the hands of AI
entries.quote: I am at maybe 3% now, much higher than a month ago.
entries.note: "Still lower than most industry people's."

entries.name: AI domain experts (XPT, n=89)
entries.role: Forecasting Research Institute, Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament
entries.label: 3% (median)
entries.scope: AI causes human extinction or reduces population below 5,000
entries.quote: The median superforecaster gives a 0.38% chance of AI-driven extinction by the end of the century, compared to 3% for the median domain expert.
entries.note: Same question as the superforecaster row. For a 10%-of-humanity AI catastrophe by 2100: experts 12%, superforecasters 2.13%.

entries.name: Matthew Adelstein
entries.quote: Liron: it all somehow maths together into 2.6%. Do you have a formula for that? Matthew: So I multiplied the probabilities
entries.note: Product of component probabilities: 90% build agents, 70% alignment by default, 70% otherwise, 60% warning shots, 80% AI could kill us.

entries.name: Metaculus community (human extinction by 2100, n=1,716)
entries.label: 2% (community)
entries.scope: human extinction from any cause, not AI-specific
entries.quote: Community prediction 2% that there are no known humans alive on January 1, 2100.
entries.note: All-cause. Was 1% in 2023.

entries.name: Scott Aaronson
entries.role: Computer scientist, UT Austin; former OpenAI alignment
entries.quote: I once gave a ~2% probability for the classic AGI-doom paperclip-maximizer-like scenario.
entries.note: Adds a "much higher" unstated probability for any AI-involved existential catastrophe.

entries.name: Michael Timothy Bennett
entries.quote: So I think without AI, our chances of blowing ourselves up are maybe 1 or 2%, and I would say 2%. And with AI, I feel like it's about half that. So 1%.
entries.note: Says AI halves his baseline; "numbers I kind of made up based on gut intuition."

entries.name: Mike Israetel
entries.scope: p(doom), as asked on Doom Debates
entries.quote: It's functionally close to zero because I take a ton of stops... So it's like each stop is 1%. Then we get 1% multiplied by 1% multiplied by 1%.
entries.note: No exact figure; "zeros repeating and then one somewhere down."

entries.name: Destiny (Steven Bonnell)
entries.quote: I would say less than one percent in the next hundred years
entries.note: Opening estimate on Doom Debates; raised to 5% by the end of the episode.

entries.name: Superforecasters (XPT, n=88)
entries.label: 0.38% (median)
entries.scope: human extinction or global population below 5,000, caused by AI
entries.quote: The median superforecaster gives a 0.38% chance of AI-driven extinction by the end of the century, compared to 3% for the median domain expert.
entries.note: Median of 88 superforecasters; domain experts in the same tournament: 3%.

entries.name: Noah Smith
entries.quote: My probability of total extinction by 2050 is so low that Daniel Kahneman would yell at me for giving a number. It's 0.1%.
entries.note: Civilizational collapse ~1%. Separately gives 96% that technology as a whole eventually ends humanity as we know it, which he doesn't necessarily consider bad.

entries.name: Dean Ball
entries.role: AI policy analyst; former White House AI Action Plan author
entries.scope: AI takes control of the world and kills large numbers of people
entries.quote: If what we're talking about is AI systems taking control over the world and killing large numbers of people... My P(doom) is very low. It's sub 1%, it's 0.01% or something like that.
entries.note: Hedged: "or something like that."

entries.name: Yann LeCun
entries.role: Chief AI scientist, Meta; Turing Award
entries.quote: Most "leading AI figures" think this p(doom) estimates are complete bullshit and the existential risk is essentially zero.
entries.note: Declines to give a figure: says all estimates are "pulled out of thin air" and it makes little sense to assign a probability to an event we have agency over. The "<0.01%" on other lists is not his wording.

entries.name: Ted Sanders
entries.quote: i fully fund my 401k and i think there's essentially zero chance AI kills all humans in the next decade.
entries.note: If wrong, "probably because I underestimate recursive self improvement."
